pattern.title: Different industries. A familiar geospatial pattern.
paragraphs: Environmental consultants, resilience teams, utilities, and location-intelligence teams ask different business questions, but the work often repeats the same underlying pattern: find or bring the right data, prepare it, run spatial analysis, check assumptions, review the result, and communicate what the map means for the decision.
GriidAi is designed to connect those steps so expert methods do not have to be rebuilt from scratch for every new project or location.

process.title: Keep the industry context. Keep the expert in control.
process.copy: Industry context changes the data, assumptions, thresholds, and interpretation of a spatial analysis. GriidAi can help organize the work and execute supported geospatial steps, but the expert still reviews the plan, checks whether the selected data and method make sense, and validates the outcome before it informs a decision.
steps: The user describes the business or spatial question.
Clarify the decision, geography, time window, and constraints.
Relevant uploaded or discoverable data is brought into the workspace.
Confirm sources, coverage, currency, and suitability.
GriidAi proposes supported analytical steps and expected outputs.
Review method, assumptions, parameters, and validation strategy.
Approved spatial operations run in the cloud workspace.
Stay within supported operations and documented boundaries.
Maps, tables, statistics, and outputs are inspected.
Decide whether the result is defensible for the intended use.
Outputs are exported and successful methods can inform future work.
Preserve context, provenance, and domain judgment.

review.title: Spatial decisions need more than a plausible map
review.copy: A spatial result can look convincing even when a projection, join, unit, time window, dataset, or assumption is wrong. That risk matters even more when the output supports environmental review, infrastructure, climate risk, or portfolio decisions. GriidAi’s human-guided approach keeps plan review and result validation visible instead of treating the first generated output as the final decision.
checks: Are the source, geography, time period, resolution, and attributes appropriate for this decision?
Are the spatial operations, parameters, CRS, units, and assumptions appropriate?
What checks should be performed before the result is accepted?
Is the output a screening result, analytical result, or decision-ready deliverable, and what additional expert review is required?

audience.title: Start with one workflow. Scale the methods that prove useful.
